gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-public-sans: Chunky, hand-cut and unfussy, Balsamiq Sans holds its line at one width with no pinched curves. Public Sans follows in a sturdy sans-serif lowercase with broad, open counters, easy going over a long passage.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-ranade: Ranade spreads its sans-serif letters wide, with stroke ends set far apart and a weight that shifts only slightly, like etched glass lines. Balsamiq Sans, hollow-looking and constant in thickness, leads above.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-supreme: Balsamiq Sans looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, moderate in lowercase height and bold in manner. Supreme sits beneath it, taller and crisper, so the page gets stencil punch above and clear text below.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-general-sans: Expressive and bold, Balsamiq Sans draws a stencil-cut line with no tight, pinched curves up top. And General Sans, a sans with a tall x-height and smooth bends, carries a longer read without any fuss.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-orbit: Orbit is a sans-serif of curves that stop short of closing, each character floating apart with a rope-like consistency in every stroke. Balsamiq Sans is the one to lean on for loud display; Orbit does the steady text work.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-syncopate: Expressive Balsamiq Sans carries a stencil-cut line with no pinched curves, while Syncopate, a sans-serif, spaces its open letters like rungs on a rope ladder. Make the heading small and the body large, and that stencil punch fades.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-manrope: Manrope is a plain sans with a bright gap at the mouth of every curve and only a small step from caps to lowercase. And Balsamiq Sans, shorter in the lowercase, gives it a bolder, hand-cut partner.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-montserrat: A stencil-cut channel of constant weight defines Balsamiq Sans, with no pinched curves anywhere. But Montserrat, a plain sans with oversized e and a counters, glides along beneath it, and that wide-open ease is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-satoshi: Balsamiq Sans cuts a bold, expressive line of constant weight with no tight curves, while Satoshi lifts a soaring x-height beneath it. But the heading is best at loud, stencil-like display, and the plain sans body at open, unsqueezed text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-switzer: Approachable and Swiss in spirit, Switzer sets tall, wire-like letterforms whose c tips never creep toward touching, under the bold Balsamiq Sans. Over many lines, its sans-serif text keeps a crisp, tubular rhythm.
